beats.text: The cookie was built for a shopping cart.
beats.note: Wikipedia says Netscape was building an e-commerce application for MCI, and MCI did not want its servers to retain partial transaction states.

beats.name: Lou Montulli
beats.role: Netscape engineer, aged 23 according to IAPP. History of Information dates the invention to June 1994.

beats.note: Wikipedia says Montulli coined the term from magic cookie, a data packet used by Unix programmers.

beats.name: Mosaic Netscape 0.9beta
beats.role: Released on 13 October 1994 with cookie support. Its first use was checking whether visitors to Netscape's own site had been before.

beats.text: It was meant to prevent tracking.
beats.note: IAPP quotes Montulli: only the originating website can set and receive the cookie, but companies figured out how to game the system.

beats.text: The advice was ignored almost at once.
beats.note: Wikipedia says the recommendation in RFC 2109, published in February 1997, was not followed by Netscape and Internet Explorer.

beats.text: A shopping cart fix became a key tool for advertising.
